searchText: b"h phase 1 — five competing architectures + theoretical file map the awtsmoos reveals many possible vessels before one becomes the chosen way; awtsmoos.com should prefer compatibility and composability over a dramatic rewrite that breaks today. architecture a — new monolithic portal api one new /api/portal/ service owns types, queries, actions, transforms, jobs, rendering metadata, and migrations. pros: obvious entrypoint, fast conceptual onboarding. cons: becomes a giant responsibility magnet; duplicates existing apis; migration blast radius enormous. verdict: reject as primary architecture. architecture b — resource envelope wrapper around existing apis add a universal resource contract library and adapters that wrap existing domain results without moving their authoritative implementation. pros: compatibility first, incremental, works with current apis, easy to test domain by domain. cons: adapter quality matters; inconsistent legacy semantics remain visible internally. verdict: strong foundation. architecture c — hypermedia capability registry a portal root/type registry publishes resource types, links, actions, schemas, representations, and capability discovery while domain apis continue handling operations. pros: frontend stops hardcoding server topology; excellent introspection and generated ui support. cons: requires disciplined link/action descriptors and compatibility mapping. verdict: combine with b. architecture d — event/graph centric everything treat all resources as graph nodes and all behavior as events/edges; ui derives from graph traversal. pros: powerful relationships/history/provenance. cons: forces simple forms/lists through an unnecessary graph mental model; risks overengineering. verdict: graph is a capability, not the universal storage abstraction. architecture e — schema/renderer plugin platform universal schema/type registry on server + renderer/field/action registry on client. specialized plugins override generic behavior. pros: unknown types remain usable; bespoke experiences remain possible; strong ui extensibility. cons: plugin precedence and security need precise boundaries. verdict: combine with b + c. chosen composite b + c + e : 1. existing apis remain authoritative. 2. a small resource domain contract library standardizes envelopes, actions, queries, errors, provenance, and capabilities. 3. domain adapters translate existing payloads into the resource vocabulary. 4. a discoverable portal root/type registry advertises capabilities and links. 5. a generic client renderer registry handles unknown/new types safely. 6. specialized domain uis progressively override generic views without abandoning the resource contract. 7. relationships, jobs, transformations, streams, and graph traversal are optional capabilities, not mandatory storage models. theoretical server file families to inspect geelooy/api/ route aggregator/entry modules. searchText: b"h phase 2 — twenty improvements after attacking the first architecture the awtsmoos gives expansion through chesed and boundary through gevurah in every instant of light; awtsmoos.com must therefore make universal possibility bounded, inspectable, cacheable, and right. 1. resource envelopes must remain deliberately small; optional capabilities belong under named sections so a basic resource is cheap to serialize and easy to understand. 2. type identifiers require namespaces and semantic versions or compatibility metadata so two domains cannot accidentally redefine post or document. 3. type definitions need explicit lifecycle states: experimental, active, deprecated, retired, with replacement links and migration notes. 4. schema recursion and deeply nested input require depth/size limits so generic rendering and validation cannot be weaponized into resource exhaustion. 5. presentation hints need a strict allowlist of semantic primitives; no arbitrary class names, selectors, html, script, or css values from untrusted api data. 6. query capability must advertise supported operators per field/type instead of accepting a universal unrestricted query language against every backend. 7. query execution requires server side maximum depth, page size, projection width, relationship traversal, aggregation cost, and timeout budgets. 8. capability discovery is advisory ui metadata; authorization must always revalidate action permission at invocation time. 9. action descriptors need stable ids separate from labels so localization and copy changes never break clients. 10. actions must declare safe/idempotent/retryable semantics explicitly; clients must not infer retry behavior from http method alone. 11. destructive actions need confirmation semantics describing whether simple confirmation, typed phrase, preview, or irreversible warning is required. 12. mutations need optimistic concurrency tokens/revisions where races matter; generic editor must surface conflicts instead of last write wins silently. 13. bulk operations need partial success receipts and item level errors rather than one global failure state. 14. error resources need safe public metadata separate from privileged diagnostics so developer inspection cannot leak secrets to ordinary users. 15. provenance must distinguish claims from verified facts; generated/inferred metadata should carry confidence/source status rather than masquerading as authored truth. 16. transformation receipts need deterministic/nondeterministic flags and hashable input/config snapshots so reproducibility claims are honest. 17. renderer selection needs deterministic precedence and diagnostics so plugins cannot unpredictably shadow each other. 18. generic rendering must impose recursion, collection length, string length, media size, and expansion limits; huge resources need lazy/paged disclosure. 19. shared css foundation must be opt in via a root attribute/class initially, then expanded only after runtime evidence; a global reset across thousands of specialized pages is too dangerous. 20. migration must prove at least one real existing domain end to end before adding broad adapters; abstractions that only pass synthetic tests are not yet architecture. resulting corrections universal means extensible contracts, not unrestricted behavior. server remains authoritative for permissions, validation, query cost, and mutation concurrency. generic ui is a safe fallback with budgets and diagnostics, not a replacement for every specialist experience. shared styling begins scoped, measurable, and reversible. existing api payloads stay stable until an adapter proves equivalence. next action write the improved phase 2 architecture around these constraints, then perform a third critique focused on evolution, caching, transport, mobile, accessibility, and operational failure.
